cuts.title: Remove the Session inventory still reachable in Task details
cuts.evidence: WorkSurfaceView.taskDetail renders Waiting and Sessions groups with counts and primary/provider/membership rows. The details sheet mounts it from SessionsContentView. This contradicts the accepted no-inventory UX; it is reachable obsolete UI, not dead code.
cuts.replacement_owner: Primary retained conversation, explicit contextual Session links and shared Waiting/program status; retain SessionRecord, full membership, TaskHistoryView and disclosed raw diagnostics.
cuts.risk: Do not lose access to a waiting secondary Session: keep an exact contextual opening path. TaskSessionGroups is exported and needs API disposition before removal.

cuts.title: Replace view-driven opening handoffs with one existing-owner handoff
cuts.evidence: SessionsContentView reacts separately to focusedPaneId, repositoryEntryReady, sessions and linkedSession, then openLinkedSession/openSession place content. WorkModel already owns request generations and SessionsWorkspaceRegistry owns retained panes. Preserve those owners; derive opening/terminal/needs-action display rather than storing another lifecycle.
cuts.replacement_owner: Existing WorkModel request identity → SessionsWorkspaceRegistry/SessionsStore → GhosttySurfacePool; stable workspace/header/pane structure and retained last-good WorkReading data.
cuts.risk: High: async stale replies, duplicate acquisition, client takeover, remote routing and unsent drafts. Generation/incarnation fences are necessary mechanics, not disposable state. This is a proposed cut, not implemented or runtime-proven.

cuts.title: Delete the unmounted native chat-reference renderer and its exclusive tests
cuts.evidence: ReferenceTextView/ReferenceContext/ReferenceMessageTextView/ReferencePopover have no production mount outside their own file. Only ReferenceTextViewTests calls static helpers. Their AppKit callbacks are protected only while the owning renderer is mounted; this closed owner is not registered by sdef or app bootstrap. resolveGitHubBase is also uncalled.
cuts.replacement_owner: Retained native provider terminal for conversations; MarkdownBlocks for authored supporting material. Exported ChatReference parser remains unresolved until library obligations are checked.
cuts.risk: Do not remove Reference-like DTOs or general attributed-text mechanics by name. UIKit-only SelectableTextView tests reference an absent production type and are historical, not active Mac proof.

cuts.title: Remove constant-nil Roadmap selection and reconnect Task clicks
cuts.evidence: RoadmapView has one initializer setting _selection = .constant(nil), yet its row callbacks assign selection and its focusedContent/workBreadcrumb/taskCard depend on non-nil. The Portfolio window still mounts RoadmapView, so deleting the entire file would remove real UI. Its Task-click assignments currently cannot navigate.
cuts.replacement_owner: Existing WavesView.openTask / repository Work navigation; keep shared legal actions, Portfolio configuration and a useful overview.
cuts.risk: Preserve access to cross-repository work. Remove dead focused branches only while wiring Task taps to the real destination; a new selection store repeats the old split ownership.

cuts.title: Remove obsolete presentation mode and stale UI-test paths
cuts.evidence: WorkNavigation.presentation defaults compact and only tests assign full; no sidebar presentation menu remains. UI tests still request work-presentation, Sessions and session-row-*; a native proof still taps debug-session-row-* despite production removal. DesktopPerformanceTests.measureWriteToVisible and measure(population:...) also locate the removed Picker, so previous performance journeys are not current acceptance evidence.
cuts.replacement_owner: One sidebar outline rule with collapse/search and unchanged retained membership; navigate tests through Work or explicit links.
cuts.risk: Do not delete retention/input tests just because their old entry path is obsolete; retarget their behavior. Keep incomplete-planning and collapsed-Wave recovery coverage.

cuts.title: Move remaining authored-Wave discovery and creation behind lf
cuts.evidence: PortfolioService already uses the lf Portfolio API. Separately, PortfolioDiscovery enumerates GOAL.md, WavesView calls WavePlanParser.objective and PortfolioRepoState.createWave writes GOAL.md/MEMORY.md. This is live split planning ownership, not a Swift SQLite reader.
cuts.replacement_owner: Rust planning/authored-Wave read and create APIs through RegistryQuery; keep explicit path validation, existing PortfolioService and historical/authored-but-unregistered evidence.
cuts.risk: Do not remove local discovery before the shared API exposes authored-only Waves and errors. No live data migration or filesystem cleanup follows from this audit.

cuts.title: Delete isolated Mac wrappers and unused view state
cuts.evidence: PlatformHelpers has no callers in either platform branch. LocalWaveAgentLauncher.interruptTask/reviewPullRequest are uncalled; their command builders have only helper-shape tests. roadmapTaskIsActionable and WorkActivityView.turnIntentError are unused.
cuts.replacement_owner: Existing concrete AppKit/Ghostty input operations and RegistryQuery Task controls; no replacement for uncalled helpers.
cuts.risk: Keep runTask/checkoutTask/controlLfPath/queryLf and their live users. A generic name match is not sufficient proof: the cut names exact module-local owners.

cuts.title: Reconcile build/resource contracts and remove stale documentation
cuts.evidence: SwiftPM enables/pins GhosttyKit, while project.yml has neither its binary dependency nor GHOSTTY_ENABLED. The disabled implementations are therefore reachable build variants. README still describes selected-skill New Session, named-Session search and old Wave Chat. DESIGN carries obsolete shortcut/prompt-authority guidance.
cuts.replacement_owner: One explicit supported build/resource contract; retain pinned patches, fonts, sdef, entitlements and shell payload until parity is established.
cuts.risk: Do not delete fallback terminal declarations solely because SwiftPM does not use them. No build/install or UI execution was performed in this audit. StatusColors.swift mixes unused aliases with the live Color(hex:) initializer: never delete the whole file based on alias use.

audit.head: 5ade59f4287558b4bdccfb8331384d4f371bd7b8
audit.scope: Every tracked *.swift repository-wide, plus every tracked non-Swift file under swift/. Source from working checkout, not generated or installed products.
audit.authority: Independent read-only relevance audit. No implementation, approval, publication, live input or migration.
accepted_ux: No extra Work tabs, primary Session breadcrumb, Session inventory or sidebar presentation menu
Rust owns planning/read APIs and execution; no Swift DB reader
Proposed stable opening-to-pane handoff and cached refresh preservation are audit criteria, not implemented behavior

parser.captured: Declarations, explicit initializers/deinitializers, named functions, extensions, per-binding variables, implicit getter bodies, explicit accessors, subscript, enum cases and every closure expression, including stored callbacks and top-level script closures.
limitations: Not a typechecked AST, compiler index, linker graph or execution trace; overloads, generic dispatch, protocol witnesses and aliases are not resolved.

Compiler-synthesized memberwise initializers, Codable/Hashable/Observable implementations, property-wrapper projections, result-builder transformations and expanded test/preview macro bodies are not separately enumerated. Their explicit owners/macros are covered; generated function completeness is not claimed.

A destructuring pattern is one binding entry, not one entry per bound identifier. Parameters, capture-list elements and closure parameters are signature content, not separately declared-function symbols.

Implicit getters are explicit inventory rows with the property binding range; they do not have separate source function declarations. Conditional paths record lexical branch clauses, not evaluated availability.
Closure call context is the nearest enclosing call expression; builder closures are included and are not all asynchronous callbacks.
Lexical reference index includes comments, strings, declaration sites and overload collisions. Empty references cannot prove deadness; dynamic owners are protected explicitly.

All tracked Swift/support files are inventoried. Semantic whole-program exhaustiveness is not claimed. Generic KEEP entries use conservative role/reference evidence, not a claim of individual runtime verification.
No app build, test suite, install, native rendering, DB read/write or external API probe was run. Binary resources are hashed/accounted for, not decoded.

token_cross_check.note: Independent all-branch SwiftSyntax token walk matches explicit func/deinit declaration inventory per file. Initializers/accessors/closures counted by typed syntax nodes, since init/get tokens also occur as expressions/identifiers.

excluded: Downloaded dependency sources and Ghostty binary internals
External/downstream SwiftPM clients not present in the checkout
audit.target_findings: 43 shared-library files, 65 Mac app files; no tracked standalone iOS app or extension target/source directory. UIKit conditional remnants are explicitly included. UI tests are XcodeGen-only.

reference_scan.note: Every per-symbol reference key links the complete Swift lexical occurrence list; per-symbol examples and external name matches are bounded display aids, not claimed full semantic call sites.
reference_scan.normalization: reference_index values and per-symbol examples are location ids; source_evidence[location_id] contains path, line, source excerpt and enclosing callable. Per-symbol candidate_count excludes the declaration line. External matches in per-symbol arrays are bounded.

review_findings: Do not replace old opening state with a second lifecycle enum/store; use existing owners and derived presentation.
No Swift SQLite reader was found; local authored-Wave discovery/writing is a separate live planning-boundary gap.
Do not delete historical Session/Process DTOs, raw debugging, Task history or native ownership mechanics merely because Session navigation is removed.
Framework entry points are preserved unless the entire unmounted owner is a manually inspected deletion cut.
No source change, release approval or acceptance proof follows from this report.
Review correction: StatusColors.swift is not a dead file. Its Color.init(hex:alpha:) has live callers; only unused exported aliases remain unresolved.

verification.test_execution: Not run: this is a read-only audit. SwiftSyntax parsing/token cross-check and artifact validation only.
verification.html_structure: balanced tags; unique ids; inline JSON parses
